blocks.text: The first step in the onboarding process is to provide the AWS organization details in the Zscaler Admin Console. DSPM uses these details to generate a template to connect to the AWS organization.

blocks.item: From the navigation menu, go to Data Security > DSPM > Cloud Accounts.
The Cloud Accounts page appears.
On the Cloud Accounts page, click Add New.
In the Select Cloud Provider window:
For Select Cloud Type, select Amazon Web Services.
For Select Onboarding Type, select Organization.
See image.
Click Next.
In the Add New Organization Configuration section:
Organization Details: Provide the AWS organization details.
DSPM Alias: Enter a user-friendly name for the organization that you want to onboard.
Role Name: Enter a unique role name. This role name is added as a prefix to all the roles that are created during the onboarding process.
Management Account Name: Enter the name of the management account. You can find this in the AWS Management Console under Organization.
Management Account ID: Enter the 12-digit AWS account ID of the management account.
Organization ID: Enter the organization ID that you want to onboard. You can find this in the AWS Management Console in multiple ways. For example:
Sign in to the AWS Management Console.
On the top right, select your account and then click Organization.
In the left-side navigation, copy the Organization ID.
See image.

Notification Emails (Optional): Enter the email addresses of the recipients who must be notified of any configuration or permissions issues encountered with the onboarded organization. You can add up to 30 email addresses of recipients. You can also add email addresses after completing the onboarding process.

External ID: View the optional identifier that is autopopulated. This ID is used in an IAM role trust policy to designate a specific user to assume the IAM role to provide access to the AWS resources. To learn more, refer to the AWS documentation.

Configure CloudTrail Integration (Optional): Select the checkbox to provide CloudTrail details. When enabled, DSPM gains read-only access to the CloudTrail logs required for incremental scans on the S3 bucket. When disabled, DSPM supports only full scans.

CloudTrail Type: Select the OrgCloudTrail checkbox, if it is an organization CloudTrail. Organization CloudTrail shares the CloudTrail events of the management and member accounts of the organization to the same CloudTrail S3 bucket.
During initial onboarding, DSPM checks for log files to perform data scan in the following paths:
After the onboarding is completed successfully, DSPM checks for log files in each target account.
CloudTrail Bucket Name: Enter the S3 bucket name that is associated with CloudTrail. This S3 bucket stores the CloudTrail events.
Prefix: Enter the prefix specified in the CloudTrail S3 bucket path.
If your CloudTrail is part of the AWS Control Tower, enter the organization ID as prefix. You can find this on the Trails page, under the Log file prefix column in the AWS Management Console.
See image.
Bucket Account ID: Enter the 12-digit AWS account ID where CloudTrail S3 bucket is present.
See image.
See image.
Click Apply to continue. Click Reset if you want to change the details.

blocks.text: If all the details are accurate, you are directed to the Connect to the Organization section to deploy the tree discovery template.
